notes: C++ keeps almost nothing about a declaration in the node that declares it. The name is at the bottom of a declarator chain — `Circle& Circle::operator+=(const Circle&)` nests a reference declarator around a function declarator around a qualified identifier, and the first named child of that is the *type* — a definition written out of line carries its class in its own name, which is what every `.cpp` in a project with headers is made of, and `declaration` is one node kind for the prototype, the global, the static member, the `using`, the `constexpr` and the `extern "C"`, which is most of what a header contains. Above all of it sits the preprocessor. An unexpanded attribute macro does not produce an error, it produces a plausible wrong tree: `FMT_BEGIN_NAMESPACE` in front of a namespace makes tree-sitter read the rest of the header as one function's body, and a body declares nothing — one token cost fmt's `args.h` all 17 of its classes and all 203 of their members. So the source is repaired byte for byte before the walk, with the spans left where they were: the macro goes where a macro is the only thing it can be (at the start of a declaration and in front of a word that can only begin one, between `class` and the name, or where `constexpr` goes in an `if`), and the delimiters of a preprocessor conditional go when its own braces do not balance — `#ifdef __cplusplus` / `extern "C" {` / `#endif` is the oldest idiom in C and it cannot be a tree-sitter node, so it takes the header guard, and the guard is the whole file. Which repair to use is decided by the parse: error bytes *plus* the bytes held in a function body that cannot be one, because the failure that matters does not show up in the error count. What the grammar still rejects is read anyway — an ERROR node is a container, and in C++ it is usually a large one: `format.h` is 168 KB of ERROR out of 170 and every class, template and function inside it is parsed whole, so they are declared, and the scope the error names (`namespace detail {`) is kept. SYMBOLS: namespaces, whether written `a::b` or nested, so a header and its source file agree; classes, structs, unions, enums and their enumerators — an unnamed enum's constants belong to the scope around it, which is what C++ says and where every bitmask enum in the corpus lives; functions and methods, declaration and definition alike, filed under the class an out-of-line name carries; constructors, destructors, operators and conversion functions, which the grammar names with punctuation and clang canonicalizes differently (`operator unsigned` is what the source wrote); fields, globals and constants; type aliases both ways round; template declarations, whose parameters bind names that are types inside them and nothing outside; `concept`; the `#define`, function-like or not, which is a declaration ctags names too; and a `friend` function, which is a declaration of the *enclosing namespace* and not of the class that granted it access. A local declares nothing — the rule a Python function's variables and a shell's `local` get. CALLS: a call, a member call through `.` or `->` (the receiver is written first, so the first named child is the object and not the callee), a qualified call, a call through a function pointer, a function-like macro, a base constructor in an initializer list — which the grammar gives the same node as a member initializer, so the file's own records decide which is which — and a construction, `Circle c(2.0)` and `vector<int> v{1,2,3}` and `new Widget()`, which is the most vexing parse and where every C++ programmer means the variable. A cast is not a call: it is written like one and what it names is a type, which is why `static_cast` was the most-called function in the corpus before the deny-list. An operator written as an operator is not one either, and that is a limit and not a choice: C++ overloads its operators and no parser without types can tell `a + b` on two ints from `a + b` on two matrices. USES_TYPE: a C++ type is a tree — `std::map<Key, std::vector<Value>>*` names three — and every level of it is a different node kind, so the whole expression is read and not one `type:` field: annotations, parameters, returns and trailing returns, template arguments, base clauses, `sizeof`, `catch`, casts, `decltype`, and the scope of a qualified name, because `std::numeric_limits<T>::max()` names `numeric_limits` and a namespace cannot take template arguments. `size_t`, `uint32_t` and the rest of the `<cstdint>` set are typedefs the grammar files under `primitive_type`; the fundamental types are a closed list and everything else under that node is a name something declared. IMPLEMENTS and EXTENDS out of the one base clause C++ writes both in: C++ has no interface keyword, an interface is an abstract class, and the only witness is `= 0` on one of its members — read directly where the base is declared in this file, and otherwise by position, because a second base in a multiple-inheritance list is a mixin and a virtual base exists to make the diamond safe. OVERRIDES from the keyword and from the base, because `override` is a keyword the language made optional and a member that redeclares a base's `virtual` overrides it whether or not it says so. EXPORTS from the three places C++ writes visibility and they disagree on purpose: the access specifier, which governs by position the way Ruby's `private` does and starts private in a `class` and public in a `struct`; `static` at namespace scope, which is internal linkage — and on a member is not that at all, it is where the member lives; and the anonymous namespace, which is the same statement in other words. IMPORTS from `#include`, by the path and by its stem without the extension, because the graph resolves a target by its last dotted segment and `shape.hpp` reduced to `hpp`; plus `using namespace` and `using X::y`, which are the only import statements the language itself has, and C++20's `import`. TESTS from the four frameworks that are the whole of C++ testing — GoogleTest, Catch2, doctest and Boost.Test — none of which has a declaration in the tree: `TEST(Suite, Name) { … }` is a function called `TEST` whose two parameters are types, and `TEST_CASE("name") { … }` is a call whose body is the next sibling. Measured against libclang on cohort 15 — fmt, googletest, json, abseil-cpp and godot's `core/` — 1,859 files and 56,000 declarations: symbols 96.5-99.8%, CALLS 96.2-99.4% over 22,000 sites, USES_TYPE 80.7-99.1%, heritage 91.5-99.0%, OVERRIDES 93.1-100%, EXPORTS 96.6-98.8% over 21,000 pairs, IMPORTS 95.5-99.7%, TESTS 83.3-97.4%. Precision: symbols 0.998-1.000, CALLS 0.945-0.998, USES_TYPE 0.985-1.000, IMPLEMENTS 0.986-1.000, OVERRIDES 1.000, and zero invented names on all five. Gap: three of them, each with its number. **The EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split is an approximation and googletest is where it shows** (0.48, against 0.83-0.95 elsewhere): an interface in C++ is an abstract class and the only witness is `= 0` on a member of the base, so a base declared in another file is read by position instead — every `class FooTest : public Test` is filed EXTENDS where clang, which has read gtest.h, says `testing::Test` is abstract because of its `virtual void TestBody() = 0`. In 169 of googletest's 185 disagreements the pair is in the graph and only the label differs. **USES_TYPE is 80.7% on json** and 91.2-99.1% everywhere else: what is left there is template metaprogramming — `enable_if_t`, `void_t`, `is_same`, `remove_reference` in SFINAE positions inside a 24k-line amalgamated header. **TESTS is 83.3% on json**, and most of that is the measure rather than the pack: a case is counted as found when it is the *origin* of a TESTS edge, and `TEST_CASE("32bit") { REQUIRE(SIZE_MAX == 0xffffffff); }` exercises nothing callable — the case is filed, it just has no subject to point at. Two of json's cases are missing from the graph outright and that part is a real gap. No fase C agent campaign.

Every declaration C makes, which is more than the grammar's node kinds say. A body is what tells a type declaration from a type *use* — `struct ops { … };` declares, the `struct ops` in `struct ops *o` does not — and reading the two the same way put a symbol in the graph for every pointer in the corpus. Functions and their prototypes as one symbol, `#define`d macros wherever written (the preprocessor has no scope, so one between two statements is still the file's), file-scope variables and constants, struct/union/enum tags, members, enumerators and typedefs, including the function-pointer typedef that is the type of every callback. `static` is the language's `private` and its absence its `public`; a type or a macro has no storage class, so what decides those is the header. IMPORTS from `#include`. USES_TYPE from the return, every parameter, every field, every local, the target of a typedef, a cast and a `sizeof`. CALLS covers the direct call and the three indirect forms that are the language's dispatch — `ops->read(f)`, `(*cb)(x)`, `handlers[i](x)` — each named by the slot, the pointer or the table it goes through, which is what a static reading of C can honestly say. EXTENDS is the first member by value: that is what makes a pointer to the outer castable to a pointer to the inner, and it is how every intrusive list, refcount base and hashmap entry in the corpus is written (`struct hashmap_entry` opens 35 structs in git). C does not distinguish that from composition — the construct is the same one — and neither does this. IMPLEMENTS is a function filling a slot of a struct of function pointers, designated or positional: `struct Curl_cftype` is filled 121 times in curl, `struct ref_storage_be` 77 times in git. OVERRIDES is a macro taking a name that already existed — after an `#undef`, over a function the file declares, or over a standard-library name. TESTS from the macro every framework writes its cases with (`TEST_IMPL`, `START_TEST`, `ZTEST`) and from the `test_*` convention, to the functions the case calls. `.h` is claimed unless the header holds C++ syntax outside comments and `#ifdef __cplusplus`: routing every header to C++ was measured on C++ projects and is right for those, but on a C project it sent the whole interface to a pack with no types. The conditionals are the one part of the preprocessor read rather than parsed around — 12.5% of the corpus's bytes fell inside an ERROR node and 43% of jq's, so a broken file is re-read with the directives blanked byte for byte (both arms kept, or the first when keeping both is what breaks), with the decoration macros a file defines to nothing expanded, and the reading that declares the most is the one kept: 0.21% of bytes left in error. Measured on five repositories (jq, libuv, redis, curl, git — 2,019 `.c` files and 920 headers) against universal-ctags for declarations and libclang for everything else. Gap: a macro's body is not parsed, so what it calls belongs to nobody; a declaration split across two arms of a conditional keeps one; cross-translation-unit linkage is by name.

Everything a shell script says about itself is written as a *command*, so almost none of it is in the grammar: `declare -A`/`-a`/`-i`/`-n` is the only place the language writes a type, `readonly`/`export` is its visibility, `alias` is a declaration, and `source` is at once its one import statement and its one inheritance. Variables are 78% of what a script declares (36,212 assignments against 9,929 function definitions over the cohort's 1,837 scripts) and none of them used to reach the graph. A declaration is script scope or an explicit `export`/`readonly`/`declare -g`; a `local` is not, the way a Python function's locals are not. `source` emits IMPORTS and EXTENDS from the one site, and takes the literal *tail* of a computed path (`source "${BASH_SOURCE%/*}/lib/util.sh"` → `lib/util.sh`), which is the idiom every shell library uses to find its own directory — two thirds of the cohort's `source` lines are literal outright. USES_TYPE is the parameter expansion, minus what the enclosing function bound itself. A wrapper (`sudo`, `env`, `time`) names both programs and `xargs` names one, because the command it runs is an argument of it. bats is read despite the grammar: `@test "name" { … }` is not syntax tree-sitter-bash has, so the headers are rewritten byte for byte into function definitions and the case keeps the description the source wrote. Measured on five repositories (bats-core, nvm, kubernetes, podman, brew) against mvdan/sh, which is a second implementation of bash, zsh and bats and not a lower bound: symbols 100/100/97/100/100% over 7,800 declarations; CALLS 97/99/94/98/97% over 14,200 sites; EXTENDS and IMPORTS 100% on all five; USES_TYPE 93-99% over 7,900 pairs; EXPORTS 97-100% over 527; TESTS 95% (bats-core, 787 pairs) and 100% (podman, 3,924). OVERRIDES is thin and exact — a name the shell already had, either a builtin or one the declaration itself wraps (`alias ls='ls --color=auto'`) — 2 of 2 on kubernetes. Gap: **zsh is a different language to this grammar** and the honest number for it is ohmyzsh's, measured on purpose and kept out of the gate: 86% symbols, 79% CALLS, 67% USES_TYPE, because 57% of its files carry syntax bash has no form of (`${(@f)…}`, `_arguments '*:: :->x'`). Also: a single-quoted string reopened mid-word (`--format='value[separator=':']('`) derails the lexer and costs 24 declarations in one of kubernetes' 4,200-line scripts; redefining a function a *sourced* file declared is an override the graph could resolve and one file cannot see; a here-document label is a delimiter and not a symbol, so ctags' 906 of them are not counted; and `eval` and a command name the shell computes name nothing on purpose.

A block is filed under the address another block writes to reach it — `aws_instance.web`, `var.region`, `local.name`, `module.vpc`, `data.aws_ami.this`, `source.amazon-ebs.ubuntu`, `dependency.vpc` — which is the block type plus its labels, with the three renamings the language performs itself, so a reference resolves with no translation table on either side. A labelled block declares at any depth (Nomad's `job`/`group`/`task`, a `dynamic`, a `provisioner`), an unlabelled one is a section of its parent, and the attributes of a `locals` are declarations of their own. CALLS from every `function_call`, provider functions (`provider::aws::arn_parse`) included; USES_TYPE from a `variable`'s `type =` (where `list(string)` is a type constructor and not a call), from the first of a block's two labels — which is where a `.tf` writes what a resource *is* — and from `provider = aws.west`; EXTENDS from a `module`/`terraform` `source` and a Terragrunt `include`, both instantiations of a parameterized configuration, and from an aliased provider to the default one; IMPLEMENTS from a Packer `build` to the sources it names; OVERRIDES from Terraform's own override mechanism — a block in `override.tf`/`*_override.tf`, an assignment in a `.tfvars` or a test's `variables`, and a second block with an address the file has already used; IMPORTS from every `source`/`path`/`config_path` and from the files `templatefile`/`file` render; EXPORTS from `output`, which is the most literal export in the registry; TESTS from the `run` blocks of a `.tftest.hcl` and from a `check`, to every address they assert on. Measured against github.com/hashicorp/hcl/v2, the language's reference implementation, over five repositories and one dialect each (terraform-aws-vpc, terraform-aws-eks, hashicorp/terraform, terragrunt, packer — 6,021 files and 15,974 declarations): symbols 1.000 in all five with zero misses, and 1.000 in all five for CALLS (1,213 pairs), USES_TYPE (2,920), heritage (498), OVERRIDES (122), IMPORTS (645), EXPORTS (683), TESTS (293) and REFERENCES (5,044). Precision re-verified against the source: symbols, CALLS, USES_TYPE, OVERRIDES and IMPLEMENTS 1.000 in all five, zero invented symbols, localization MRR 1.0. Because both ends of a call and of a type reference are known to that parser, those are exact figures and not lower bounds. Gap: a provider schema is not read, so the type of a resource (`aws_instance`) and the attribute a reference reaches through (`.id`) are external names; `count`/`for_each` are not expanded, so `aws_instance.web[0]` and `aws_instance.web["a"]` are one address; a reference into a module's outputs resolves to the `module` block and not to the `output` inside the module it sources; a rendered `.tftpl` is not indexed as a language of its own; the JSON spellings (`.tf.json`, `.tfvars.json`) are JSON and are not claimed; no fase C agent campaign.

Classes, objects (a singleton, not a second class of the same name), traits, enums and their cases, type aliases, givens, `def`s, `val`/`var`s and the parameters of a `case class`, which are its public fields. Backticks are quoting and not part of a name — lila's generated i18n table is 2,541 of them and keeping the quoting made every one unfindable. EXTENDS for the first parent of an `extends` clause and IMPLEMENTS for every `with` after it, plus `derives` and a `given … with`; a self-type (`self: Cache =>`) is DEPENDS_ON, because it constrains what may mix the trait in rather than naming a parent. CALLS from all three shapes Scala has — application, selection (`xs.sum`, uniform access) and infix application (`a |+| b`) — minus the symbolic operators the standard library defines on primitives and collections, which name nothing anybody looks up. USES_TYPE from every annotated position and not only signatures: parameters (both lists — a `def` gives its type parameters and its value parameters the same field name, and reading the first skipped the second), return types, `val`/`var` ascriptions, bounds, `new`, `asInstanceOf[…]`, a typed pattern, a lambda's parameters and an annotation, which is a class. IMPORTS as the dotted path the source wrote rather than its segments. TESTS from a ScalaTest/munit/specs2 suite to the subjects its cases call, the suite recognised by its framework base or by the *Spec/*Suite/*Test convention. Measured against Scalameta, the language's reference parser, on five repositories (os-lib, cats-parse, cats-effect, zio, lila — 51,000 files): symbol recall 100% on all five; CALLS 92-97%; USES_TYPE 96-99.5%; heritage 96-100% and the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split itself 98.6-100%; IMPORTS 91-100%. Gap: implicit and given *resolution* — which instance the compiler picks at a call site is not modelled, only that the instance exists and what it implements; macros and `transparent inline` expansions; overload resolution, so two `map`s in one repository resolve by name; a companion object and its class share a name path and so share a canonical id, which means an edge one of them carries is attributed to whichever the graph interned (archis#544) — the two are one namespace to a reader, but asking which of the pair extends something can answer for the other; and no fase C agent campaign, which is the only thing between this and Stable.

Every declaration a container makes, which in Zig is nearly everything: the language writes its types, its constants, its module aliases and its re-exports all as `const`, and only the scope separates one from a local. Functions, container fields, the members of an `error{}` set, `test` blocks named without their quotes. `pub`/`export` → EXPORTS, `@import` → IMPORTS, signatures and field types → USES_TYPE. Zig has no inheritance keyword — `usingnamespace` was removed in 0.15 and survives once in the 3,251 files of the bench corpus — so derivation is read from the three idioms that replaced it: comptime instantiation (`const L = ArrayList(u8)`), the embedded base attested by `@fieldParentPtr`, and the vtable that fills an interface. OVERRIDES is container scoping. Measured against `std.zig.Ast`, the compiler's own parser, over five repositories: symbols 1.000 on four and 0.998 on ziglang/zig, CALLS 0.972-1.000, USES_TYPE 0.923-1.000, heritage 0.930-1.000, OVERRIDES 1.000 on 105 pairs. Gap: names a `comptime` block computes, `@field`/`@hasDecl` reflection, and a base recovered through a pointer whose type only the annotation names.

Lua keeps almost everything it means outside its grammar, and the pack reads all three places it keeps it. Symbols: functions in the three forms the language has — `function M.encode(t)`, `M.setup = function()` and a function inside a table constructor — keeping the table they hang off (`M.encode`, `M:method`); the classes a `---@class` declares with the fields a `---@field` lists, including the blocks that document no statement at all (71 of nvim-lspconfig's 851 files are `---@meta` and hold nothing but annotations); and the keys of a chunk-level table one level deep, which is what `return { cmd = …, filetypes = … }` is and the whole content of 763 of that repository's files. USES_TYPE from LuaCATS (`@param`, `@return`, `@type`, `@field`, `@cast`, `@alias`), because Lua has no type syntax and this is the same trade JavaScript's JSDoc makes; both spellings are read, `---@x` and `--- @x`, because neovim's own runtime writes 480 of the first and 339 of the second. EXTENDS from the four ways Lua writes inheritance — `---@class Dog : Animal`, `setmetatable(Dog, Animal)`, `setmetatable(Dog, { __index = Animal })`, `Dog.__index = Animal` — plus `Object:extend()`, which is rxi/classic and what every class library in the ecosystem copies; `Dog.__index = Dog` is the idiom that makes a table its own index and is not inheritance. OVERRIDES is a method on a table that inherits. EXPORTS is `return M` or `return { … }`, the only statement the language makes about visibility. TESTS are busted's `it(…)` cases, which are calls and not declarations. IMPORTS from `require`, recorded by the path written and by its last segment, because `require("lspconfig.util")` names a file whose symbols hang off `util`. A `.rockspec` is a Lua chunk and is indexed as one. Measured on five repositories — neovim, nvim-lspconfig, plenary.nvim, Kong, lazy.nvim, 29,493 declarations — against luaparser and not universal-ctags, whose whole Lua parser is one kind (`f  functions`): symbol recall 100% on all five with three residual misses in the whole cohort, CALLS 99.6-99.9% over 39,876 pairs, heritage 100% on the four that have any (333 pairs; plenary reports none because it writes `X.__index = X` fourteen times, which is the right answer), USES_TYPE 99.4-100% over 5,586 pairs, OVERRIDES 100% over 72, EXPORTS 98.7-100% over 3,601. Precision on the same five: symbols 0.998-1.000, CALLS 0.970-0.993, USES_TYPE 0.993-1.000, heritage 1.000 over 349 sampled edges, OVERRIDES 1.000 over 150, and not one of the five invents a symbol (five fabricated names, no hits). The keys of a configuration table are the one cost: they are per-file names that repeat across a repository — nvim-lspconfig declares `cmd` 763 times — so localizing one by name drops to 62% strict Top-5 there against 88-99% on the rest of the cohort. The trade is a name that is not unique for a file that used to declare nothing. Gap: a `---@class N` written above `local M = {}` names one table twice and the two are not linked, so a method on `M` misses the override it makes on `N`'s base; the local alias a `require` binds is not resolved, so a qualified call is recorded both as written and by its last segment and resolution picks between them; `---@generic` yields no type; and no agent-level campaign, which is what separates this from Stable.

Elixir has no declaration syntax. `defmodule`, `def`, `defstruct`, `defprotocol` and `defimpl` are macros, so every declaration parses as a call — and so does every `case`, `for` and `with`. What tells them apart is the name in the target, not the node kind, and the other half of what a module says about itself is written in its attributes, which is why this is a pack (`elixir_source`) and not a table. Symbols: modules named the way the language names them (`defmodule Inner` inside `A` is `A.Inner`; a `defimpl` is `Protocol.Type`, absolutely, wherever it is written); protocols; `def`/`defp`/`defmacro`/`defguard`/`defdelegate`, including the operators Kernel defines as `defmacro left and right`; the fields of a `defstruct`; the types of `@type`/`@typep`/`@opaque`; the callbacks of `@callback`; the constant a bare `@name value` binds, which is what Elixir has instead of a `const`; and ExUnit's `test`/`describe`/`setup`, named by the string the compiler decoded and found wherever they stand, an `if` around them included. A function written as five clauses is one symbol; two arities are two. USES_TYPE from `@spec`, `@type`, `@callback` and `%Struct{}` — a function head carries no types at all, so those four are the whole dimension. IMPLEMENTS from the five ways the language writes inheritance, none of them a clause: `@behaviour`, `defimpl … for:`, `@derive`, `defexception` (which injects `@behaviour Exception`) and `use`, which also emits EXTENDS because it runs a macro that splices code in — that is why a Phoenix controller answers to functions no file declares. OVERRIDES from `@impl`, resolved against the module's `@behaviour` when it is written `@impl true`, and from every function of a `defimpl`. EXPORTS is `def` against `defp`, which is the whole of the language's visibility. IMPORTS from alias/import/require/use, with `alias A.{B, C}` counted as the two modules it names. A dot is a call when its receiver is a module and a field when it is a variable: `Repo.all(q)` is one and `conn.assigns` is not. Measured against `Code.string_to_quoted/2`, the compiler's own front end rather than a second implementation, over five repositories — plug_crypto, ecto, phoenix, elixir/elixir and plausible-analytics, 42,097 declarations: symbols 1.000 on four and 0.999 on elixir/elixir (18 misses in the cohort), CALLS 0.986-1.000 over 105,212 sites, heritage 0.986-1.000 over 2,769 pairs, USES_TYPE 0.986-1.000 over 5,447, OVERRIDES 1.000 over 288, EXPORTS 0.984-1.000 over 8,292. Precision on the same five: symbols 0.993-1.000, CALLS 0.985-1.000, USES_TYPE 0.907-1.000, OVERRIDES 0.972-1.000, IMPLEMENTS 1.000 on all five, and not one of them invents a symbol (five fabricated names, no hits). Gap: a protocol implementation for a type declared in another file records the implementation module's edge and not the type's, because that edge would start at a symbol this file does not have; what a `use` splices in is named nowhere, so `defoverridable` and the function that replaces it are never paired; a module whose name a macro computes (`Module.concat`, `defmodule unquote(name)`) has no name until the macro runs, which is 7 of elixir/elixir's 19,574; and no agent-level campaign, which is what separates this from Stable.

Classes, structs, enums, actors and extensions, split by the keyword the one `class_declaration` node kept; protocols and their requirements; stored and computed properties, including the `let a: Int, b: String` that declares two; `init`, `deinit` and `subscript`, which the language names with the keyword and the grammar does not name at all — a subscript's `name:` child is its *return type*, which is what made every subscript in a repository a symbol called `Int`; operators, precedence groups and macros; enum cases; type aliases and associated types. A `let` inside a function body binds a local and is not a declaration. EXTENDS and IMPLEMENTS out of the one comma-separated list Swift writes both in: only a class may name a base and only in first place, and whether that first name is a base or a protocol is decided by what the file declares, by the standard library's and Cocoa's protocol names, and by the `-able`/`-ible`/`-Delegate`/`-DataSource` convention. An enum's raw value type (`enum D: String`) is not heritage, and a suppressed conformance (`~Copyable`) is the opposite of it: both are USES_TYPE. EXPORTS from the visibility keyword — `open`/`public`/`package` leave the module, `internal` (which is what no keyword means) and the two `private`s do not; `public private(set)` is a public property whose setter is private; a member of a `public extension` and a requirement of a public protocol are public without saying so. USES_TYPE from every type position, which this grammar hides in a child whose *field* is `name` — the same field a declaration's own name uses — so the generic signature pass, which asks for a field called `type`, reached none of them: annotations, return types, generic parameters and their constraints, `where` clauses, `as`/`is` casts, and a property wrapper or global actor, which is a type written as an attribute. CALLS from a call, from a construction written with generic arguments (`Mutex<Shell?>(nil)`, a node of its own) and from a macro expansion, but not from a compiler directive — `#line` is a value and `#available` is a condition. OVERRIDES from the `override` keyword wherever it is legal: a method, a computed property, an `init`, a `subscript`, and a protocol that redeclares an inherited `associatedtype`. IMPORTS as the module, not the attribute of an `@_exported` re-export nor the member of an `import struct Foundation.Data`. TESTS from XCTest, whose cases are named and not annotated, and from swift-testing's `@Test`. Measured against swift-syntax, the parser the compiler front-ends with, on five repositories (swift-argument-parser, Alamofire, swift-collections, swift-nio, swift-composable-architecture — 2,345 files, 48,841 declarations): symbol recall 99.8-100%, which the report rounds to 100% on all five (12 residual misses in the whole cohort); CALLS 99.6-100% over 67,419 sites; USES_TYPE 98.2-100% over 21,479 references; heritage 98.5-100% over 4,011 pairs and the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split itself the same; OVERRIDES 100%; EXPORTS 95.3-100%; IMPORTS 100% on all five. Precision: symbols 1.0, IMPLEMENTS 1.0 and OVERRIDES 1.0 on all five, CALLS 0.90-0.98, USES_TYPE 0.91-0.96, and no invented edge. Archis parses Swift with its own fork of tree-sitter-swift (crates/tree-sitter-swift-archis): the published grammar left an ERROR node in 222 of those files, and a file with one declares nothing after it. Gap: 88 files still hold one — the lifetime attributes, `borrow`/`mutate` accessors, a generic `typealias` with a `where` clause and the case-path operator; `MemoryLayout<Key>.stride` parses as two comparisons, which is the `<` ambiguity every non-typechecking parser has; overload resolution, so two `map`s in one repository resolve by name; and no fase C agent campaign, which is the only thing between this and Stable.

Ruby's grammar says less about a Ruby program than any other grammar in this registry, and the pack reads the four places the language says it instead. SYMBOLS: classes, modules, methods and singleton methods; the constants an assignment declares (`VERSION = "1.0"` — 1,523 of Homebrew's, 87 of jekyll's), and what it declares depends on the value, so `Class.new(B)` is a class that extends B, `Struct.new(:a, :b)` is a class with two accessors and their writers, `Module.new` a module; the methods `attr_reader`/`attr_writer`/`attr_accessor` put on a class (2,412 in the cohort), the writer named `x=` as Ruby names it; `define_method`, `alias_method`, `alias`, and ActiveSupport's `delegate`. `class << self` is deliberately NOT a declaration: it reopens the singleton of whatever encloses it, so its methods belong to that scope — read as a class it took its first method's name as its own and buried the method a level deeper. CALLS: everything, because in Ruby everything is a method call — `require`, `include`, `attr_reader`, `private` and `raise` are calls, and each is recorded both as the call it is and as the edge it means. Including the ones no parse tree can see: a bare word with no receiver, no arguments and no parentheses is a call on `self` unless a local variable of that name is in scope, and the grammar gives a variable read and a method call the same node, so the pack reconstructs the scope — 8% of every call in the corpus is of that shape. `f.(x)` is a call to `call`. USES_TYPE: Ruby has no type syntax and writes its types in three other places at once — Sorbet's `sig { params(x: Integer).returns(Foo) }` (7,894 blocks in Homebrew), YARD's `@param [Foo]` / `@return [Foo]` (1,318 tags), the RBS-inline `#:` annotation — plus every constant the source refers to, because a Ruby constant is a type name. There is no primitive deny-list on either side of the measurement: `String` and `Integer` are ordinary classes here and half the ecosystem reopens them. EXTENDS from `<` and from `Class.new(B)`; IMPLEMENTS from `include`, `prepend` and `extend` — every argument, and only with a bare receiver, because `@obj.extend M` extends that object and not the class the line sits in. OVERRIDES: `super` is the language's own witness and Ruby needs no keyword for it; a base that declares the same name in the file is the second witness. EXPORTS: there is no export clause, so what a class exposes is whatever a bare `private` or `protected` has not taken away — in statement order, three statements up, with nothing in the tree marking the methods it caught (2,147 of them here) — plus `private :x`, `private_constant` and `private_class_method`. `private` governs methods only: a constant and a nested class written after one are still public, and a `class << self` body starts public again. TESTS: RSpec's `it`/`specify`/`example`, minitest's and Rails's `test "…"` (9,107 in rails), shoulda's `should "…"` (898 in jekyll, which writes no `it` at all), and the `def test_…` convention. IMPORTS from `require`/`require_relative`/`load`/`autoload`, whose target is the file and not the constant it will define — except for ActiveSupport's one-argument `autoload :Base`, which infers the path from the constant and is 559 of rails's. Measured against Prism, the parser Ruby itself ships, over five repositories — dry-monads, github/secure_headers, jekyll, Homebrew/brew and rails, 5,648 files and 69,966 declarations: symbol recall 100% on all five (116 residual misses in the whole cohort), CALLS 100% on all five over 144,487 pairs, USES_TYPE 100% over 35,794, heritage 100% over 7,900 pairs with the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split measured on its own and also 100%, OVERRIDES 99.7-100% over 1,366, EXPORTS 99.9-100% over 57,518, IMPORTS 99.9-100% over 10,837, and Prism refused none of the 5,648 files, so no row of the cohort rests on a file only one of the two could read. Precision on the same five, verified against the source: symbols 1.000 on all five, IMPLEMENTS and OVERRIDES 1.000 on all five, CALLS 0.980-1.000, USES_TYPE 0.975-1.000, and not one of the five invents a symbol (five fabricated names, no hits). What is left of it is one cause: an instance method and a class method of the same name share a symbol id, so a repeated `class Operation` in a spec file collects the edges of all three. One grammar hole, repaired: an endless method whose body is a paren-less call (`def value! = raise UnwrapError, self`) has no rule in tree-sitter-ruby 0.23.1 and the recovery takes the enclosing modules with it, so the arguments past the first are blanked byte for byte and the declaration, its callee and its first type reference survive. Gap: `method_missing` and the methods a `class_eval` string defines are invisible by construction; a Rails DSL (`has_many :posts`) puts methods on a class that this does not name; `T.type_alias` reads as a constant and not as a type; an instance method and a class method of the same name share one symbol id, so an edge on either is attributed to whichever the graph interned (archis#544); and no agent-level campaign, which is what separates this from Stable.

A document declares by writing an identifier something else reaches it by, and that is the whole of the model: an `id`, which the format makes unique and which a script, a stylesheet, a `<label for>` and an `href="#x"` all use to find the element; a control's `name`, which is what the server reads the field by; a `<meta name>`/`http-equiv` key; a `<slot name>`, a `<template id>` and a named anchor; a heading and the `<title>`, which is what the page calls itself and what a fact about the whole page hangs off. Nothing else is a symbol — a `<div>` with no name says nothing its parent did not already say — so there is no depth cap and no symbol for a bare tag. The other half of a document is the two languages written inside it. A `<style>` is read as CSS: a rule declares the classes it styles (a class has no other definition site) and the custom properties it sets, points at the ids it selects, and overrides the rule whose selector it repeats. A `<script>` is read with the JavaScript pack over a copy of the document with everything that is not script blanked out, so every span it reports is a span of this file and the whole document costs one parse per group of scripts rather than one per script; a script belongs to the element it is written inside, which is how django's `jsi18n.html` puts twelve of them in twelve different paragraphs. CALLS from an `on*=` handler (parsed, not scanned: `onclick="return confirm(msg)"` is not a statement JavaScript accepts at the top level), from the body of an inline script, and from the endpoint a `<form action>`, a `formaction` or an `hx-get`/`hx-post` names — which is how a page invokes a server. USES_TYPE from `class=`, which is the type of HTML and in a themed page most of what the markup says, from a tag with a hyphen (the one type the language has of its own) and from a `{{ value }}` a template reads. REFERENCES from the one cross-reference the format resolves itself: `for`, `list`, `form`, `headers`, `popovertarget`, the nine `aria-*` idrefs and an `href="#id"`. IMPLEMENTS from `role=`, which is the interface an element says it implements — the contract the accessibility tree, the keyboard handling and the assistive technology all read it by. EXTENDS from the page being another page with its holes filled (`{% extends %}`, `{{ define }}`), because half the `.html` in a repository is a template and the file name is the only thing that says which. OVERRIDES is one rule in four shapes: a `<meta>` key written twice, a selector of the stylesheet repeated, a `style=` beating a rule of the document that selects that element, and a `{% block %}` filling the hole its layout left. IMPORTS from `<script src>`, `<link href>`, the media elements, an `@import`, an ES module `import` and a `{% include %}` — an `<a href>` is deliberately not one, because a link is somewhere to go and not something the page loads. EXPORTS is what the page makes reachable: an `id`, a control name, a block, and a declaration at the top level of a *classic* script, which lands on `window` where the same declaration inside a `type="module"` lands nowhere. TESTS because a document can be a runner, and its cases are calls whose subjects are what their bodies reach for — the treatment mocha's `it(…)` gets in JavaScript and bats's cases get in Bash. `test` and `it` are read in any inline script, the way they are in a `.js`; `async_test` and `promise_test` are testharness.js's and nothing else's, so they are read only where the document says it loads a harness. Measured against html5lib (the WHATWG tree-construction algorithm), tinycss2 and acorn on bootstrap, htmx, aria-practices, AdminLTE, web-platform-tests and django's templates — 4,196 documents, 24,890 declarations: symbol recall 1.000/1.000/0.996/0.997/0.996/0.995 and structural 1.000 on five of six; CALLS 0.996-1.000 over 14,206 sites; USES_TYPE 0.989-1.000 over 17,747 pairs; heritage 1.000 over 726 pairs with the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split at 1.000; REFERENCES 0.995-1.000 over 2,170; IMPORTS 0.988-1.000 over 10,243; EXPORTS 0.983-1.000 over 14,797; OVERRIDES 1.000 over 124; TESTS 0.938-1.000 over 6,386. Precision on the same six: symbols 0.983-1.000, CALLS 1.000, USES_TYPE 1.000, IMPLEMENTS 1.000, OVERRIDES 0.995-1.000, and not one of the six invents a symbol. Gap: an attribute whose value holds an unescaped quote — `title="{% translate "Run" %}"`, which a template engine writes and HTML does not allow — is tokenized differently by the two parsers and costs that element; markup written to be illegal on purpose (a `<select>` inside an `<option>`) is read literally rather than restructured the way the spec says, which is three documents of web-platform-tests; a character reference outside Latin-1 and Latin Extended-A that is not written numerically is left as it was written, which costs that name; a resource is named by its file name, so two `util.js` in two directories are one name and nothing resolves a URL; `.css` is not indexed, so a class used here and declared in an external stylesheet resolves by unique name like any other cross-file edge; the customized built-in `is=` is claimed and appears in none of the 4,196 documents, so EXTENDS rests on the template notations; a `{% %}` contributes only `extends`, `include` and `block`, because a statement is not an expression and reading it as one made a variable out of every `{% endblock %}`; shadow DOM and `<template>` content are read as ordinary markup, with no scoping; and the JavaScript inside is read by the JavaScript pack, so that pack's gaps are this one's — OVERRIDES among them. No fase C agent campaign.

A TOML document declares nothing with a keyword: it writes an address between brackets, and that address — `tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies` — is at once the symbol's name, its scope and the string anything else uses to reach it. So a table, an array-of-tables element, a pair at any depth and the intermediate tables a dotted key implies are all symbols, each named by its full address; an array-of-tables element is named by its own `name` where it has one (`[[bin]]` → `bin.chi`), the way a Kubernetes object is named by its `metadata.name`, and by its position where it has none. The order the document writes them in carries nothing — `[a.b]` may precede `[a]` — so the whole file is read before one edge is emitted. CALLS from the two things a manifest can invoke: a shell command line (`[build] command`, a `[tasks]`/`[scripts]` entry, a Cargo `[alias]`), split on the shell operators the way a Dockerfile `RUN` is; and an entry point (`chi = "archis.cli:main"`), whose function is the CALLS and whose module is the IMPORTS. USES_TYPE from a value that names an address this same document declares — resolved as TOML resolves one, as a key of the same table, a sibling of the table, a whole address written out, or Cargo's explicit `dep:` — and from the `$VAR`/`${VAR}` a value expands. EXTENDS from `inherits`/`extend`/`base` and their spellings, which is what `[profile.release] inherits = "dev"` says. IMPLEMENTS is the specialization: a table addressed `s₀…sₙ` fills the schema of `s₀…sₖ` + `sₙ` for the longest prefix the document declares, which is `[dependencies]` for `[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]` and `[tool.poetry.dependencies]` for `[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]`. OVERRIDES is exact and not inferred: it is every key the specializing or inheriting table writes that the general one already declares, computed from two known key sets, plus an address the document declares twice. IMPORTS from a dependency table's entries, from a requirement list (`requires`, PEP 621's `dependencies`), and from the file a `path`/`include`/`extend`/`build` names. EXPORTS because the format has no visibility: a document's public surface is its top-level addresses plus the entries of the tables that exist to be read from outside (`[features]`, the scripts, the entry points). TESTS from `[[test]]` and `[[bench]]`, from a table that configures a test runner (`[tool.pytest.*]`, `[tool.coverage.*]`, nextest, tox, nox), from a task named for the tests, and from a dev-dependency — which Cargo defines as being for tests, examples and benchmarks. Measured on five repositories, one per dialect (cargo, rust, ruff, poetry, starship — 1,182 documents and 25,958 declarations) against tomllib, the TOML 1.0 parser of the Python standard library, which answers exactly rather than as a lower bound — so TOML's recall joins XML's, proto's, GraphQL's and CSS's in not being a floor: symbols 1.000 on all five, with one residual miss in the whole corpus, a manifest cargo's own test suite writes in order to be rejected; CALLS 1.000 over 67 sites, USES_TYPE 1.000 over 1,149 pairs, IMPORTS 1.000 over 1,672, heritage 1.000 over 84 (EXTENDS and IMPLEMENTS pooled), OVERRIDES 1.000 over 63, EXPORTS 1.000 over 653 and TESTS 1.000 over 222. Precision 1.000 on every measured dimension of all five, and not one of them invents a symbol. Gap: an internal edge resolves by the trailing segment of its address, and a manifest's addresses all end in the same handful of words — `name`, `version`, `dependencies`, `features` — so a target with two candidates is recorded as ambiguous rather than decided, and the address the source wrote is carried untouched beside it; a quoted key that holds a dot (`["a.b"]`) is not told from the dotted header `[a.b]`, because a canonical name joins its segments with that same character; a document TOML itself refuses — a duplicate key, a bad escape — is still read through the grammar's error recovery, so Archis and a conforming parser disagree by construction on a manifest that is invalid on purpose, which is what cargo's and ruff's test suites are full of; a value that names an address of *another* document is not an edge — a `workspace = true` points at the workspace root's `[workspace.dependencies]` and nothing in this file says where that file is; the shell split is an operator split and not a shell parse, the same one a Dockerfile's `RUN` gets; a generated lock file is not read at all — `Cargo.lock`, `poetry.lock` and `uv.lock` are TOML and their extension is not, so nothing claims them, which is the intent and does mean a resolved dependency graph is not in the index; and no fase C agent campaign.

A Haskell declaration is two nodes and not one: the type signature and every equation are siblings carrying the same name, so `foldr` with five equations is one `signature` node and five `function` nodes side by side. The symbol is their union — the span of all of them, the type from the signature beside them — and reading them as a table of node kinds declared that function six times, each copy holding a fragment of what the source said. What is a symbol: the module, every top-level binding, `data`, `newtype`, `type`, the type and data families, their constructors in all three notations and their GADT form, their record fields, `class` and its methods, `instance` and its definitions, pattern synonyms, `foreign import`/`export`, and the `where` and `let` bindings inside all of them, which are most of what a Haskell function is made of. **The class is the interface and the instance is the implementation**, and that is the whole of the language's hierarchy: no subclasses, no virtual methods, nothing that extends a type. So IMPLEMENTS is `instance C T`, every name in a `deriving` clause under any of the four strategies, a standalone `deriving instance` and a family instance filling its family — one relation with five spellings — and it starts at the *type* whenever this module is where that type is declared, because "what implements this class" is the question it exists to answer. EXTENDS is the superclass, which the language writes as a *constraint* (`class Eq a => Ord a`) and not as a clause, plus the representation type a `deriving newtype` inherits its instances from. OVERRIDES is exact and computed from two known name sets, never from a convention: an instance method against the `default` its class wrote — the one thing in Haskell that means what OVERRIDES means everywhere else here — and a local binding against the top-level name it shadows. CALLS reads a name referred to as a name called, because in a language where application is juxtaposition and composition is an operator the expression that *names* a function and the one that *applies* it are usually not the same: `map area xs` never writes `area` in head position and `render = pack . show` writes no application at all. So every name in expression position is a call site — the head of an application, the infix operator (which is a function like any other: `$`, `.`, `<$>` and `>>=` are most of what the language writes), the operator a section names, and a bare reference — except a name a *pattern* bound, which is a value and names no declaration. A `where` binding is not one of those: it is a declaration, it is a symbol, and calling it is an edge. USES_TYPE from every type constructor written in a signature, a context, a data declaration, a constructor pattern, an expression annotation, a type application and an instance head, with the type *variables* left out because they name nothing. IMPORTS keyed by the trailing segment of the module path and reported by the whole of it, with what a `hiding` names left out. EXPORTS from the export list — and **a module that writes no list exports everything it declares**, which is the opposite of almost every other language's default; `T(..)` carries the constructors and the fields with it, and an instance is named in no export list because it travels with the class and the type it joins. TESTS because none of the four frameworks declares a test: an hspec `it`, a tasty `testCase`, a QuickCheck property and an HUnit `~:` are calls, and what the case is a test *of* is what its body reaches for minus the vocabulary every case is written with. A `.lhs` is read too, in all three of its notations — Bird tracks, the Report's `\begin{code}` and the Markdown fence `markdown-unlit` reads — with the prose blanked byte for byte so every span is a span of the file on disk; nothing in a literate file says which notation it uses, and a `>` opening a line is code in one and a block quote in another, so both readings are parsed and the one that declares the most is kept. Measured on five repositories and five dialects of the language (containers, aeson, servant, hspec, pandoc — 1,019 documents and 43,183 declarations) against **GHC's own parser**, `GHC.Parser.parseModule` over a `StringBuffer`, which stops where tree-sitter stops and makes the recall exact rather than a floor: symbols 1.000/1.000/0.999/0.998/0.998 and structurally the same; CALLS 0.996-0.998 over 109,180 sites; USES_TYPE 0.966-0.998 over 53,636 pairs; heritage 0.958-1.000 over 3,385 pairs, with the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split at the same figures; IMPORTS 1.000 on all five over 1,015; EXPORTS 0.998-1.000 over 4,854; TESTS 0.984-0.996 over 2,541; OVERRIDES 1.000 over the 25 an instance takes from a class default in the same file. Precision: symbols 0.99-1.000, CALLS 0.950-0.983, USES_TYPE 0.990-1.000, IMPLEMENTS 0.968-1.000, OVERRIDES 0.918-1.000 wherever there are enough of them to mean anything (pandoc writes two), and not one of the five invents a symbol. universal-ctags 6.2.1 does have a Haskell parser and it is not an oracle: four kinds, and on containers' `Data/Map/Internal.hs` — 4,600 lines and 444 symbols — it emits one tag, for a module whose name it truncates to `Data`. Gap: **tree-sitter-haskell is a preprocessor, not a parser around one** — its `cpp` node swallows the `#else` arm whole, so a conditional whose arms are declarations is merged byte for byte before the grammar sees it (`Data.Graph`'s portable `SetM` monad, its three instances and its seventeen bindings live in one), and a conditional *inside* an expression is left alone, because merging that breaks the layout and lifts a function's `where` bindings to the top level; a lone `#if` with no second arm is never merged, since the grammar already keeps the only arm there is. A macro the preprocessor would have expanded is not expanded, so what it names belongs to nobody. OVERRIDES is only ever emitted where both name sets are in the file, which is most of what makes it exact and also most of what it misses: a class in another module is not consulted. The `deriving` of a class this repository does not declare resolves by unique name like any other cross-file edge. A type is not *checked*: an instance is named by its class and the head constructor of its first argument, so two instances the language tells apart by a later argument are one name here. The 13 modules of the 974 that GHC itself refuses are a fact about the corpus — a preprocessor macro standing where a declaration goes, an extension the `.cabal` turns on and the file does not — and they are out of the denominator rather than counted as empty, as are the 41 literate documents, which the pack reads and the oracle does not. And no fase C agent campaign.

There are no declarations in R, there are assignments: the grammar has no `function_declaration` node and the language has no `def`, so `f <- function(x) x` is a `binary_operator` whose right-hand side happens to be a function and `n <- 42` is the same node with a number there instead. What a name *is* depends on what is on the other side of the arrow, and `<-`, `<<-`, `=`, `->`, `->>` and `assign("f", …)` are one declaration written six ways. What is a symbol: every binding in all six, at the top level and inside every body; the parameters of a function with their defaults; the classes of all four of the language's object systems with their slots, fields and methods; the generics; the S3 and S4 methods; and the cases of a test file, which testthat writes as a description and a block and never as a name. And the generic is the interface, but **a method names itself by convention rather than declaring anything**: `print.data.frame` is the `print` method for class `data.frame` and nothing in the syntax says so, so splitting it needs to know which prefixes name a generic — the ones the file declares with `UseMethod`, the ones roxygen names outright with `@method`, the ones a NAMESPACE registers with `S3method`, and, for everything every package extends, a table derived from R itself by walking the namespaces of `base`, `stats`, `utils`, `graphics`, `grDevices`, `methods`, `tools` and `parallel` for the functions that dispatch on their own name. IMPLEMENTS is that method against its generic, a `setMethod` against its `setGeneric`, and a class against the virtual class it `contains` — which is the language's own word for an interface. EXTENDS is `contains =` (S4 and reference classes), `inherit =` (R6), the second argument of a `ggproto`, and the tail of the class vector a `class(x) <- c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")` or a `structure(…, class = …)` writes, which is how an S3 class comes into being at all and is its whole inheritance chain in one expression. OVERRIDES is exact wherever the file holds both halves of the evidence and is never a naming convention: a method that calls `super$f()`, `callSuper()`, `callNextMethod()` or `NextMethod()` is saying outright that it replaces one, a member of a subclass that names a member its base declared replaces it, and a local binding repeating a top-level name shadows it. CALLS is the call node, the `%…%` operators — which are functions and nothing else, since no primitive is spelled that way — the `obj$method()` of both reference systems, and the function handed to a `do.call`, an `lapply` or a `purrr::map`, marked dynamic because what runs is a value and the name beside it is the evidence. USES_TYPE has four sources and the language writes a type nowhere else: an S4 slot's declared class, a `setMethod` signature, the class a `new`/`as`/`is`/`inherits`/`validObject`/`structure`/`class<-` names, and the class half of an S3 method's identifier. IMPORTS is `library`, `require`, `requireNamespace`, `source`, every `pkg::fun`, roxygen's `@import`/`@importFrom` and the `import()` lines of a NAMESPACE — which is R source and is claimed as such, because it is the one file of a package that says what the package exports. EXPORTS is roxygen's `@export` family and a NAMESPACE's `export()`/`S3method()` lines, and a file that writes neither exports everything it declares that does not begin with a dot, which is the language's own rule for what is private. An `.Rmd`, a `.qmd` and an `.Rnw` are read too, with the prose between the chunks blanked byte for byte so every span is still a span of the file on disk. Measured on five repositories, one per object system (dplyr for S3, ggplot2 for ggproto, shiny for R6, data.table for base R with a hand-written NAMESPACE, S4Vectors for S4 and reference classes — 1,037 documents and 32,460 declarations) against **R's own parser**, `parse()` over the language objects it returns, which stops where tree-sitter stops and makes the recall exact rather than a floor: symbols 1.000 on all five with no miss at all; CALLS 0.994-0.996 over 48,385 sites; USES_TYPE 0.984-1.000; heritage 1.000 on all five, with the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split at the same figure; IMPORTS 0.974-1.000; EXPORTS 0.997-1.000; TESTS 0.987-0.995; OVERRIDES 0.926-1.000. Precision: symbols 0.983-1.000, CALLS 0.890-0.958, USES_TYPE 0.963-1.000, IMPLEMENTS 0.890-1.000, OVERRIDES 1.000 on all five, and not one of them invents a symbol. universal-ctags 6.2.1 has an R parser and it is not the oracle: its ten kinds are ten shapes of *assignment*, so a `setClass` is a call it has no opinion about, an `R6Class` member list is one `list` tag, and the relationship between `print.myclass` and `print` does not exist as far as it is concerned. Gaps. OVERRIDES is only emitted where both name sets are in the file, which is most of what makes it exact and most of what it misses: a class whose parent is declared in another file is not consulted. An S3 method whose generic is neither in this file nor in base R reads as a function with a dot in its name, which is the right answer far more often than not — `check.input` is not a method — but is the wrong one for a package generic used in a file that does not declare it. The arithmetic and comparison operators are deliberately not calls: they are primitives that dispatch only when an operand carries a class, so an edge to `+` would name the primitive and not the `Ops.myclass` that may or may not run. A hidden directory is not indexed, which on data.table is the 298 declarations of its `.ci/` and `.dev/` scripts. And no fase C agent campaign.

Objective-C writes down everything it means and the grammar names almost none of it. A method has no name at all: the selector is spread over the declaration's children, one keyword before each argument, so `- (void)setX:(int)x y:(int)y` is called `setX:y:` — and reading the first identifier called it `setX`, which is a different method's name and collides with every other `setX…` the class declares. The same name is at the other end of every edge, because a message writes its *receiver* first: `[array addObject:x]` came out a call to `array`, and a message is the only way this language calls a method, so that was every call in it bar the C functions. SYMBOLS: classes, protocols and their requirements, and categories named the way the language names them — `NSString(MyAdditions)` is a declaration of its own and not the class, which is what it used to be called and what collected every method a third party adds to it; a class *extension*, the anonymous `@interface Foo ()` a `.m` writes for its private half, is the opposite case and keeps the class's name, because that is what the language means by it. A `@property`, whose name is not a child of it either — the grammar reuses C's field declaration and puts the attribute list in front, so every property in the language came out named after its first attribute — plus the accessors it declares, which are the names the rest of the repository sends; a declaration that names several at once (`@property Foo *a, *b, *c;`) declares all of them. Ivars with their own visibility; `@synthesize` and `@dynamic`; `@compatibility_alias`; the `NS_ENUM`/`NS_OPTIONS` that is how an enum is really written here, whose name is the macro's second argument and not a node the grammar names — and the same shape written with a project's own macro, because `typedef IDENT(…) {` is an enum in C and nothing else; `#define` and `#define f(x)`, which is where a header keeps its constants; the `NSString * const kFooKey` that is the only way this language has to name a key; and the block typedefs a callback API is written in. CALLS from a message, from a C call, from `@selector(…)` — which names a method without sending to it — and from dot syntax, which is a message to an accessor: `view.frame` is `[view frame]` and `view.frame = r` is `[view setFrame:r]`, and that is how most sends in modern code are written. USES_TYPE from every position the language writes a type in, which is all of them: a method's return and parameter types, a property's, an ivar's, the lightweight generics of `NSDictionary<NSString *, id<NSCopying>> *`, the protocol qualifier of `id<Drawable>`, a cast, and the receiver of a class message, which is the commonest type reference in the language and the one Clang itself reports as one. EXTENDS from a superclass and from a category to the class it is written on; IMPLEMENTS from every conformance list — a class writes its own in `parameterized_arguments`, the same node as its generic parameter list, and only *position* separates them, while the node named `protocol_reference_list` is a protocol's own inheritance and the qualifier of a type, which is why reading that one made every `id<Drawable>` annotation a conformance and left no class conforming to anything. OVERRIDES needs no keyword because the language has `super`: a `[super sel]` in the body carrying this method's own selector, and, where the file shows the base, a superclass or an adopted protocol that declares the same selector — a protocol and the class that implements it are conventionally written in one header, which is where both are in hand, and redeclaring a `@property` a protocol requires overrides the two methods it requires. EXPORTS is the most literal rule in the registry after HCL's `output`: what a `.h` holds is public and the same declaration in a `.m` is not, which is written in the file's name and nowhere in its text — narrowed by `static`, by an ivar's own `@public`/`@protected`/`@private`, which runs by position the way Ruby's `private` does and cannot make an ivar more visible than the declaration around it, and by a class extension being private by construction wherever it is written. IMPORTS from `#import`/`#include` and from `@import`. TESTS from XCTest, whose cases are named by convention rather than annotated, so what identifies one is the base class, followed through the chain because a repository that puts its shared `setUp` in an abstract base and subclasses it twice is the common case. Two holes in tree-sitter-objc 3.0.2 put an ERROR node over 35% of the cohort and both have one shape — a bare macro word alone on its line is read as the *type* of a declaration and the ERROR it opens covers the rest of the file (`NS_ASSUME_NONNULL_BEGIN` is that word in 643 files), and `typedef NS_ENUM(NSUInteger, Name) { … }` leaves the type's name as an argument in a parameter list — and a third hole produces no error at all: the nullability and covariance keywords Clang reserves and this grammar has no rule for turn `ASDK_EXTERN __kindof ASDisplayNode * _Nullable ASFind(…)` into a multiplication whose right operand is a call, which is a plausible tree with no declaration in it. All of them are rewritten byte for byte before the walk, so every span still points where the file says it does, and the reading kept is the one that *declares the most* rather than the one with fewest error bytes — a `#ifndef` inside an `@implementation` costs every method in it without costing one byte of error. Measured against libclang, the compiler's own front end, over five repositories chosen for size and for dialect — AFNetworking, SDWebImage and CocoaLumberjack for the language as it is usually written, Texture because it is Objective-C++ almost throughout, which is the dialect the `mm` extension claims and which nobody had measured, and firebase-ios-sdk because it keeps C, C++ and Objective-C headers in one tree under one extension, which is what the header rule has to get right — 3,450 files and 38,187 declarations: symbol recall 0.990-1.000 on all five, 273 residual misses in the whole cohort; CALLS 0.950-0.996 over 49,269 sites; USES_TYPE 0.957-1.000 over 11,813; heritage 0.981-1.000 over 1,911 pairs, with the EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS split measured on its own at 0.982-1.000; OVERRIDES 0.939-1.000; EXPORTS 0.927-0.995 over 10,616; IMPORTS 0.990-1.000 over 9,360. Precision re-verified against the source on the same five: symbols 0.995-1.000, CALLS 0.985-0.998, USES_TYPE 0.990-1.000, OVERRIDES 0.945-1.000, IMPLEMENTS 1.000 on all five, localization MRR 1.0, and not one of them invents a symbol (five fabricated names, no hits). Clang compiles for the host, so it reads one arm of a `#if` where this pack reads both, and 396 of the 3,450 files are ones it would not parse at all: every figure above is measured on what the two can both see, and nothing outside that is credited to either side. Gap: an override whose base is declared in another file or in the SDK is not recorded and is not counted — `viewDidMoveToWindow` over `NSView` and a protocol requirement whose protocol is in another header are overrides the language knows about and a per-file reading cannot; `objc_msgSend`, `performSelector:` and a selector built by `NSSelectorFromString` are the dynamic call and name nothing, so nothing is invented for them; what the preprocessor pastes together is written nowhere, so neither side counts it; a `.mm` that is mostly C++ is read by this pack and not by the C++ one, which is where the residual ERROR bytes are; and no fase C agent campaign, which is the only thing between this and Stable.

Arrow-functions + CommonJS `X.prototype.m=fn`/`app.m=fn`/`exports.f=fn` + object-literal methods + `require()` IMPORTS + named function expressions + the keys of `module.exports={…}` and of a module-level enum object, with EXPORTS edges for the export list. TESTS from `it(…)`/`test(…)` to the subjects the case calls — 920 edges on express, 924 on eslint — because jest and mocha have no test declaration to mark. USES_TYPE from JSDoc (`@param {SourceCode}`, `@type {import('…').RuleModule}`) and from every construction site, which is the source that does not depend on anyone annotating: 53% of files carry a type layer at the median of the five cohort repositories (14% express, 41% axios, 53% mongoose, 67% eslint, 84% winston), against 38-40% for Python and 49% for TypeScript, both of which the registry rates `Yes` on the same measure. Precision 0.95-0.997. A class written as an expression — `module.exports = class C extends Base {}` — is a class. Measured on five repositories: structural recall against universal-ctags 100% (express), 98% (axios), 100% (eslint), 96% (mongoose), 99% (winston); CALLS recall 95/98/96/98/92%; heritage 100% (axios), 99% (mongoose), 100% (winston). Gap: no static types; an anonymous callback is not a declaration, so the calls inside one are attributed to the file; the tree *under* an exported object is data and is not indexed — which is most of what the pooled ctags figure still counts.
IMPORTS(use)/USES_TYPE/EXPORTS(pub)/#[test] + `impl Trait for T` → IMPLEMENTS (246 on ripgrep). Gap: associated items, blanket/generic impls, macro-generated code.
Agent-benchmarked. Gap: extension-function/overload resolution; IMPLEMENTS vs EXTENDS split.
EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS/OVERRIDES + IMPORTS/USES_TYPE + @Test. Gap: overload resolution, Spring DI, generated sources.
Gap: partial classes, events/delegates, IMPLEMENTS vs EXTENDS split.

Classes, traits, interfaces, enums, records; methods typed and `def`, constructors, fields and properties; script-level functions and bindings. EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS from the clauses, including a trait in an `implements` list; OVERRIDES from `@Override`; IMPORTS from `import`, `import static` and `import x.*`, as the path with its last segment as the resolution key rather than as one edge per dotted segment; USES_TYPE from field, parameter and return types, from generics minus their arguments, from every construction site, and from a type named in a body — `o as Widget`, `(Widget) o`, `o instanceof Widget` — where a signature pass never looks. TESTS from `@Test` and from a Spock feature method, which is a `def` whose name is a sentence in quotes and carries no annotation at all. And the DSLs, which is most of the Groovy anybody writes: a task is a declaration (`task jar(type: Jar)`, `tasks.register('jar', Jar)`) and the type it names is EXTENDS; a Jenkins `stage('Build')` is a declaration; DEPENDS_ON from a plugin (`plugins { id … }`, `apply plugin:`), from a dependency coordinate with its version dropped, and from a script's `@Grab`; `configurations`, `ext` and `sourceSets` entries are declarations because the block they sit in says so. Measured over 21,412 files of spock, grails-core, apache/groovy, gradle, ratpack and elasticsearch. Gap: a command whose first argument is a regex literal (`rename ~/(.*)\.zip/, …`) still splits into two statements; `dependsOn packageDocs` is told from the declaration `Certificate chain` by Groovy's capitalisation convention and not by the grammar, which cannot tell them apart; a Spock spec that embeds a whole build script in a triple-quoted string is the string it is; a property write (`archiveFileName = …`) is not an edge; no fase C agent campaign.
IMPORTS/USES_TYPE/TESTS + base-class EXTENDS + module-level bindings. Gap: decorators as relations, `__all__` re-exports, dynamic edges.

EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS + IMPORTS/USES_TYPE, properties and class constants. The corpus holds 103 PHP files and 55 of them declare nothing, so the figure is a thin sample; Guzzle on its own measured 99% under the stricter, pre-#228 metric. Gap: PSR-4 autoload, service container, magic methods.
TSX grammar + arrow-functions + type-aliases + module-const + object-literal methods. Gap: import-alias calls, decorators, conditional types.
Agent-benchmarked (v3.1–v3.4). Implicit-interface IMPLEMENTS via method-set matching (71 inferred on gin) + receiver→type association. Gap: embedding-promoted methods, pointer vs value receiver.

A rule is a symbol named by its selector, because the selector is what another stylesheet, another rule or a `querySelector` writes to reach it — the same reason an HCL block is named by its address. Resolved, not as written: a rule nested inside another is named by what the `&` resolves to (`.card` + `&:hover` is `.card:hover`), and a rule inside a condition is named by its selector under the at-rule that conditions it, so the `.btn` under a `@media` and the `.btn` outside it are the two rules they are. **The custom property is the other half of the language**: 62% of what the corpus declares is a `--name` in a value position (84,368 of bulma's 135,286 declarations), and none of them used to reach any graph. Also `@keyframes`, `@font-face` — named by the `font-family` it gives itself, which is the one declaration in CSS that names itself from the inside — `@property`, `@layer`, `@custom-media`, `@custom-selector`, `@namespace`, Tailwind's `@utility`, and the conditional at-rules (`@media`, `@supports`, `@container`, `@scope`) as the scopes their rules sit in. An at-rule no dialect of CSS claims is read as a rule would be, so a `.css` file written in PostCSS or Tailwind still declares what it declares. CALLS from every function in a value — `calc`, `clamp`, `color-mix`, the gradients, the transforms — with `var()` and `url()` excluded because neither is a call: one names a custom property and the other a file, and each carries the kind that says so. USES_TYPE from `var(--x)` and its fallback, from a custom function (`--theme(…)`), from `animation`/`animation-name` to the `@keyframes` it names (identified in the shorthand by elimination, as a browser identifies it), from `font-family` to the `@font-face` family minus the generic keywords, from a `@media (--md)` to the `@custom-media` that declared it, from `layer(x)` in an `@import`, from a `@container` name and from Tailwind's `@apply`. EXTENDS is the selector that refines another — a state, a part, an attribute, one more class attached to a selector this file also declares — and the nesting, which is the same relation written the other way round; 28,236 of bulma's selectors refine another and 4,791 pairs survive the rule that the base has to be declared here. OVERRIDES is the cascade, and it is the only thing in CSS that decides between two declarations: a refining selector that re-declares a property its base already set, or the same selector re-declared inside a condition. Computed from the two property sets, never guessed — and `!important` is not consulted, because what the edge says is that the two rules collide and not which one a browser picks. IMPORTS from `@import`, and from the string-argument at-rules a `.css` file really carries (`@plugin`, `@source`, `@reference`, `@use`) — which tree-sitter-css has no form for, so the statement is blanked byte for byte and read from the text, because left in it takes the selector of the rule after it. DEPENDS_ON from a `url()` that is not a data URI: the fonts, images and masks a stylesheet needs, and the only thing in a stylesheet that is not CSS. EXPORTS is the public surface — the custom properties declared on the document root plus every name an at-rule declares — because CSS has no modules and "everything is exported" would be true and useless. Measured on five repositories (bulma, animate.css, open-props, tailwindcss, Font-Awesome — 260 stylesheets, 106,000 declarations) against tinycss2, an implementation of CSS Syntax Level 3 written from the specification: symbols 100% on all five, and CALLS, USES_TYPE, EXTENDS, OVERRIDES, EXPORTS, IMPORTS and DEPENDS_ON 100% on every repository that writes them; precision 1.000 on all five dimensions of all five, zero invented. Gap: `tests` is `No` because CSS has no test construct — `@supports` is feature detection, not an assertion — and claiming one would be claiming a syntax the language does not have. A refinement whose base is declared in another file is not an edge: with a flat namespace and no imports, `a:hover` would otherwise inherit from every `a` in the repository. The cascade is recorded and not ranked: layer order, specificity and source order decide the winner and the edge says only that the two rules conflict. A shorthand is not expanded, so a `transition-delay` that overrides a `transition` is not counted. `@media`'s query is matched as written, so two spellings of one breakpoint are two names. And no fase C agent campaign.

Messages, enums, enum values, services, rpcs, fields, map fields, a oneof and its variants, the fields an `extend` block declares and proto2 `group`s — at any nesting depth — plus the `package` clause. CALLS from an rpc to its request and its response; USES_TYPE from a field's type, a map's value type, an rpc's request/response and the extension a custom option names, minus the fifteen scalars; EXTENDS from an extension field to the message it re-opens; OVERRIDES where a declaration shadows an enclosing scope; IMPORTS from the import path, `public` and `weak` included; EXPORTS for every top-level declaration. Relations are measured against protoc's own `FileDescriptorSet` rather than a regex, which makes proto the second language after XML whose CALLS and USES_TYPE recall are exact and not a lower bound. Gap: no cross-package resolution — a reference resolves by its trailing segment, so two packages that both declare `Status` are one target; tree-sitter-proto 0.4 has a rule for neither `extensions N [declaration = {…}]` nor `group`, and both are recovered from what it leaves behind — a `group` is rewritten into the `message` it is, so the field it also declares is named by protobuf's rule (the group's name lowercased) rather than written anywhere in the file, and is the one symbol in the corpus whose name does not appear in its own span; no fase C agent campaign.

An element that names itself is a declaration at any depth — `<xs:complexType name=>`, `<xsl:template name=>`, `<target name=>`, `<bean id=>`, `<select id=>` — with a Maven coordinate read from element text (`<artifactId>demo</artifactId>`) and the tag as the name of last resort, capped at four levels of structure. CALLS from `<xsl:call-template>`, Ant `depends`, MSBuild `DependsOnTargets`/`<CallTarget>`, a Maven `<goal>` and a MyBatis `<include refid=>`; USES_TYPE from `type`/`ref`/`itemType`/`memberTypes`/`as`/`class`, minus the XML Schema built-ins; EXTENDS from `<xs:extension base=>`, `<xs:restriction base=>`, `<bean parent=>` and a POM's `<parent>`; IMPLEMENTS from `substitutionGroup`; OVERRIDES inside `<xs:redefine>`/`<xs:override>`; IMPORTS from `schemaLocation`/`href`/`<Import Project=>`/`<import resource=>`/`<module>`; DEPENDS_ON from a POM's dependencies and plugins. Gap: no namespace resolution — a prefix is stripped rather than bound, so `type=` is matched by the element it sits on and two dialects that use one local name for different things are separated by the prefix and not by the namespace it points at; a schema that declares its own type named after an XML Schema built-in loses that edge; a document that is not UTF-8 is not indexed at all, which for XML is a real case because XML is the format that declares its own encoding; no fase C agent campaign.

One symbol per build stage (`FROM x AS y`, and an unnamed stage under its base image), with the ARG/ENV variables and LABEL keys scoped to the stage that declared them. EXTENDS when a `FROM` names an earlier stage of the same file, IMPORTS when it names an image (and from a `# syntax=` directive); DEPENDS_ON from `COPY --from=<stage>` and `RUN --mount=…,from=<stage>`, which is how a runtime stage takes what a builder made — the same syntax naming an image is an IMPORTS instead; CALLS from every command a `RUN` body runs — split on the shell operators outside quotes, with comment lines dropped before the continuations are joined, `${…}` and `$(…)` skipped whole and the substitution walked for the program inside it, naming a wrapper like `sudo` and what it runs — and the same for `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT`/`HEALTHCHECK CMD`, the instruction inside `ONBUILD` and the script of a `<<EOF` heredoc, which the grammar keeps in a block of its own; USES_TYPE from `$VAR`/`${VAR}`, in an instruction, in a flag value (`--mount=…,id=build-$TARGETPLATFORM`) and inside a `RUN` body, where the grammar leaves them as text; OVERRIDES when an `ARG`/`ENV` redeclares a name its stage can already see, from an ancestor stage or from the global `ARG`s before the first `FROM`. Gap: the shell split is an operator split and not a shell parse — it reads a `$(…)` substitution but not a backquoted one, and a `$CMD` held in a variable is deliberately not guessed at rather than pointed at a program that does not exist; an image reference is matched as written, so `node:20` and `node:20-alpine` are two names and nothing resolves a registry or a digest; a `--from=` that names neither a stage nor an image (a build context passed on the command line) is read as an image; a comment trailing an `ARG` makes the grammar swallow the instruction after it, which costs that instruction's edges; no fase C agent campaign.

A mapping key is a name the document wrote, so a key is a symbol down to three levels of structure — past that is payload.
