Exempt from the cap, and therefore a declaration at any depth: an anchor (`&base`), a mapping named by its own `name:` (a workflow step, an Ansible task, a Kubernetes container or env entry), a Kubernetes object named by its `metadata.name` — which is the document's subject, and what a fact about the whole document hangs off — and a key that redefines something merged in. An anchor is emitted beside the key it was written under, because that is what an alias resolves to. EXTENDS from the merge key `<<: *base` (and from a sequence of them), from Compose's `extends: {service:}` and from GitLab CI's `extends:`, all three being the same idea; OVERRIDES when a key beside one of those was already supplied by what it inherits, computed against the parent's real key set and not guessed; IMPLEMENTS from `kind:`, guarded on `apiVersion` so that only a cluster object claims one. CALLS from a `run:`/`script:` shell fragment split the way a Dockerfile `RUN` is, from a `command:`/`entrypoint:`/`args:` read as argv when it is a sequence and as a shell line when it is a scalar, from the module an Ansible task names, and from a Helm `include`/`template`. IMPORTS from `uses:`, `image:`, `env_file:` and Ansible's `include_tasks`/`import_playbook`; DEPENDS_ON from `needs:` and `depends_on:`. USES_TYPE from an alias (`*base`), from `${{ env.X }}`/`secrets`/`inputs`/`matrix`/`needs`/`steps`, from `{{ .Values.x }}` and a bare Jinja variable, from `${VAR}`, and from the Kubernetes references written as a `name:` under a `…Ref` (`configMapKeyRef`, `secretKeyRef`) or as `serviceAccountName`/`claimName`/`secretName`. Gap: no schema awareness past `kind:` — a key is read by its name and not against an OpenAPI or CRD schema; a Helm *template* is usually not well-formed YAML and does not parse at all, so what is read of that notation is what survives inside a document that does; the Ansible module rule is guarded on the mapping being an item of a task list with a `name:`, so a task written without one keeps its module unread; `exports`/`tests` are `No` by construction; no fase C agent campaign.

Types, interfaces, enums and their values, inputs, unions, scalars, directives, fields, field arguments, input fields, operations and their variables, fragments, the `schema` block and all seven `extend`s. CALLS from a fragment spread, from a field selection (the resolver it names) and from an applied directive; USES_TYPE from a field/argument/variable type with `!` and `[]` peeled off, from union members, from a fragment's type condition and from the root operation types, minus the five built-in scalars nothing declares; IMPLEMENTS from the implements list, including an interface implementing an interface and an `extend type` that adds one; OVERRIDES where a field is also declared by an interface the type implements, resolved across the document. Gap: `imports`/`exports`/`tests` are No because GraphQL has none — the `#import "./f.graphql"` convention some toolchains layer on top appears in zero of the 795 documents of the benchmark cohort, so it is left unclaimed rather than declared for a case the corpus does not contain; no schema stitching either, so a fragment or type defined in another file resolves by unique name like any other cross-file edge and OVERRIDES under-reports when a type and its interface live in different files; a selection is matched to a field by name and not against the schema, so two types with a same-named field are one target; and the grammar refuses the occasional definition the reference parser accepts (one field of one type in apollo-kotlin's 468 KB Studio schema), which used to dissolve the rest of the file into loose tokens and now costs only that definition — 184 of apollo-kotlin's 11,580 type edges, and nothing anywhere else in the cohort. Measured against graphql-core on apollo-kotlin, graphql-java, saleor, graphql-js and apollo-client: symbols 100% on all five; CALLS 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.999/1.000; USES_TYPE 1.000 except apollo-kotlin's 0.984; IMPLEMENTS and OVERRIDES 1.000 throughout. No fase C agent campaign.
